subject.title: after_tool_call hook receives a flattened string, not the structured ToolResult — plugins cannot detect exec/bash failures

question: Should OpenClaw canonicalize Codex-native shell/apply_patch `after_tool_call` payloads from app-server completion data instead of forwarding Codex's raw string `PostToolUse` response as the plugin-visible result?
rationale: The defect is clear, but the repair changes the public plugin hook payload and timing boundary, so maintainers need to choose between native-relay immediacy, structured fidelity, duplicate avoidance, and string-result compatibility.

options.title: Canonical structured OpenClaw payload
options.body: Use app-server commandExecution/fileChange completion data as the plugin-visible result for Codex-native shell/apply_patch, suppress the raw duplicate, and keep a documented text/output field for display consumers.

options.title: Wait for upstream Codex structure
options.body: Keep the current relay contract and require Codex to emit structured shell/exec `tool_response`, accepting that this OpenClaw issue remains blocked until that ships.

options.title: Document raw string as contract
options.body: Declare the current raw-string result intentional and direct plugins to another outcome surface, leaving exit-code observability outside `after_tool_call`.

recommendation.title: Canonical structured OpenClaw payload
recommendation.body: Use app-server commandExecution/fileChange completion data as the plugin-visible result for Codex-native shell/apply_patch, suppress the raw duplicate, and keep a documented text/output field for display consumers.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision changes the public plugin hook/tool-result contract boundary connected to #71021, with Codex app-server owners implementing whichever direction maintainers choose.
